learning_goal: Know the heart's valves, its own blood supply, and the great vessels entering and leaving it.
gaps: The four chambers have no separate models in this source set - the chambers are taught here through their valves and papillary muscles. Resolve true chamber models from the fuller upstream archive when the self-host ingest runs.
No aortic valve model exists in this source set (mitral, tricuspid and pulmonary do).
No pericardium model exists in this source set - the pericardium half of this topic is narration-only until then.

structures.name: wall of heart
structures.label: Heart (myocardium)
structures.narration: The muscular wall itself — thickest around the left ventricle, which drives blood to the whole body.

structures.name: tricuspid valve
structures.label: Tricuspid valve
structures.narration: Between the right atrium and right ventricle — three cusps, held by the papillary muscles.

structures.name: mitral valve
structures.label: Mitral valve
structures.narration: Between the left atrium and left ventricle — two cusps, on the high-pressure side.

structures.name: pulmonary valve
structures.label: Pulmonary valve
structures.narration: Guards the exit from the right ventricle into the pulmonary artery.

structures.name: anterior papillary muscle of right ventricle
structures.label: Papillary muscle — anterior, RV
structures.narration: Pulls on the chordae to stop the tricuspid cusps prolapsing when the ventricle squeezes.

structures.name: posterior papillary muscle of left ventricle
structures.label: Papillary muscle — posterior, LV
structures.narration: Its blood supply is single in most hearts — which is why it fails after an inferior infarct.

structures.name: ascending aorta
structures.label: Ascending aorta
structures.narration: Leaves the left ventricle — the coronary arteries branch from its very first centimetre.

structures.name: arch of aorta
structures.label: Arch of aorta
structures.narration: Arches back and to the left, giving off the vessels to the head and the arms.

structures.name: descending aorta
structures.label: Descending aorta
structures.narration: Continues down behind the heart against the vertebral column.

structures.name: pulmonary artery
structures.label: Pulmonary artery
structures.narration: The one artery carrying oxygen-poor blood — right ventricle to lungs.

structures.name: pulmonary vein
structures.label: Pulmonary vein
structures.narration: The one vein carrying oxygen-rich blood — lungs back to the left atrium.

structures.name: superior vena cava
structures.label: Superior vena cava
structures.narration: Brings blood back from the head, neck and arms into the right atrium.

structures.name: inferior vena cava
structures.label: Inferior vena cava
structures.narration: Brings blood back from everything below the diaphragm.

structures.name: stem of left coronary artery
structures.label: Left coronary artery
structures.narration: A short stem off the aortic root that divides almost immediately.

structures.name: circumflex branch of left coronary artery
structures.label: Circumflex branch
structures.narration: Curves left around the heart in the coronary groove to supply the left side.

structures.name: trunk of right coronary artery
structures.label: Right coronary artery
structures.narration: Runs right in the coronary groove — supplies the SA and AV nodes in most people.

structures.name: marginal branch of right coronary artery
structures.label: Marginal branch
structures.narration: Runs along the sharp lower border to the right ventricle.

structures.name: great cardiac vein
structures.label: Great cardiac vein
structures.narration: Runs beside the anterior interventricular artery and drains into the coronary sinus.

structures.name: coronary sinus
structures.label: Coronary sinus
structures.narration: The heart's own venous return, emptying straight into the right atrium.

views.title: See it in the body
views.narration: The heart sits in the middle of the chest, tilted so its tip points down and to the left, behind the sternum.

views.title: Among its neighbours
views.narration: It nestles between the two lungs, above the diaphragm, with the great vessels rising from its top.

views.title: Inside — the valves
views.narration: Cut it open and the four chambers are defined by their doors: tricuspid and pulmonary on the right, mitral on the left, each held shut by the papillary muscles.

views.title: How it works — one beat
views.narration: Blue blood arrives through the venae cavae, past the tricuspid, out the pulmonary valve to the lungs; it returns red through the pulmonary veins, past the mitral valve, and is driven out the aorta to the body.

views.title: Its own blood supply
views.narration: The coronary arteries branch off the aortic root and wrap the heart to feed the muscle itself; the cardiac veins return that blood through the coronary sinus.
